![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14056541/assets/75df54dd30da590814e89153396ac7cf8a713fc9a6e04d14786780147ba57cfe.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(5,-1),$ and passes through the point $(17,11).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(5,-1),$ and so we have

$$
x-5=p{t}^{2},\,y+1=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(17,11),$ we can substitute $x=17$ and $y=11$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}12=p{t}^{2} \\ 12=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =2pt \\ 6 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{6}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =p{(\frac{6}{p})}^{2} \\ 12 & =p\cdot \frac{36}{{p}^{2}} \\ 12 & =\frac{36}{p} \\ p & =\frac{36}{12} \\ p & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-5=(3){t}^{2},\,y+1=2(3)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-5=3{t}^{2},\,y+1=6t.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of Parabola Given Its Parametric Equations
questions.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x-3=-6t,\,y-1=-3{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =-\frac{x-3}{6},\,{t}^{2}=-\frac{y-1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(-\frac{x-3}{6})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-\frac{y-1}{3}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{36} & =-\frac{y-1}{3} \\ (x-3)^{2} & =36\cdot (-\frac{y-1}{3}) \\ (x-3)^{2} & =-12(y-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(3,1),$ and passes through the point $(-5,-7).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(3,1),$ and so we have

$$
x-3=p{t}^{2},\,y-1=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(-5,-7),$ we can substitute $x=-5$ and $y=-7$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}-8=p{t}^{2} \\ -8=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =2pt \\ -4 & =pt \\ t & =-\frac{4}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =p{(-\frac{4}{p})}^{2} \\ -8 & =p\cdot \frac{16}{{p}^{2}} \\ -8 & =\frac{16}{p} \\ p & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-3=(-2){t}^{2},\,y-1=2(-2)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-3=-2{t}^{2},\,y-1=-4t.
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation $(y+1)^{2}=-(x-3)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h)$ that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),$ we see that the parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(3,-1).$ So we have

$$
x-3=p{t}^{2},\,y+1=2pt.
$$

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4p(x-h) & =-(x-3) \\ 4p(x-3) & =-(x-3) \\ 4p & =-1 \\ p & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-3=(-\frac{1}{4}){t}^{2},\,y+1=2(-\frac{1}{4})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-3=-\frac{1}{4}{t}^{2},\,y+1=-\frac{1}{2}t.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following parametric equation of the parabola 

$$
x+2=5t,\,y-2={t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

The Cartesian equation of this parabola is

$(x\,+$
{{field-1}}$)^{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{x+2}{5},\,{t}^{2}=y-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(\frac{x+2}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=y-2$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{25} & =y-2 \\ {(x+2)}^{2} & =25(y-2)\end{aligned}
$$
